exposure: Nulliparous women with single cephalic, term pregnancy, and spontaneous labour
Women from South and Central Asia
cohort: 48,711 women who gave birth in a Local Health District in Australia between 2011 and 2015
finding: Caesarean section rates varied by country of birth and within some Robson groups, suggesting that both maternal origin and obstetric factors influence the likelihood of caesarean delivery.
mod_finding: This study found variations in cesarean section rates among immigrant populations in Australia, with South and Central Asian women having higher rates even after adjusting for demographic and clinical factors.
